answer: On 7 October 2023 Hamas-led fighters attacked southern Israel. About 1,200 people were killed, most of them civilians, and about 250 were taken to Gaza as hostages. The counts come mainly from the Israeli government. Human Rights Watch found that the attackers committed war crimes and crimes against humanity, including murder of civilians and hostage-taking. A UN commission of inquiry and the UN human rights office found war crimes. A UN team led by Pramila Patten found reasonable grounds to believe sexual violence took place, but its visit was not a full investigation. Hamas says its fighters targeted soldiers and that any harm to civilians was accidental. A parent can say: Amnesty International, which accuses Israel of genocide, also condemned the attack for deliberate mass killings and hostage-taking.

facts.text: Hamas's own account, in its document 'Our Narrative... Operation Al-Aqsa Flood' (21 January 2024), is that the operation targeted Israeli military sites and that its fighters 'only targeted the occupation soldiers and those who carried weapons'; it says avoiding harm to civilians is a religious and moral commitment, that any targeting of civilians happened accidentally, and that 'maybe some faults happened'. The findings in the other facts on this card are that the attacks were directed against civilians.

contested.text: Counts differ by source. The Israeli government reported 1,195 deaths; the UN human rights office cited more than 1,124, including 295 military personnel; AFP, in a count described by Human Rights Watch, found 815 of the 1,195 to be civilians and did not count soldiers, police or community security teams as civilians, although some police and rapid response members are civilians under the laws of war.

contested.text: Some people were killed by Israeli forces. The UN human rights office reported that some Israeli civilians were killed by fire from Israeli forces in the course of fighting, and the UN Commission of Inquiry reported that in several locations Israeli forces applied the so-called 'Hannibal directive' and killed at least 14 Israeli civilians. Human Rights Watch says that, where it could tell, only a minority of civilian deaths came from fighting with Israeli forces, and that it found no evidence for the claim that most deaths came from heavy weapons only Israeli forces use.

not_claimed: This card does not say that every claim made about 7 October is proven; the Patten mission and Human Rights Watch both called for further investigation of sexual violence.
It does not say anything about the conduct of the war in Gaza that followed.
It does not say Palestinians in general are responsible for the attack.
It does not say the counts are final; they are the figures given by the Israeli government and checked by Human Rights Watch and the UN.
could_not_verify: The UN Commission of Inquiry's full report on 7 October (PDF) could not be read; its findings are cited from UN News and the UN human rights office update report.
The OHCHR press release on the Commission's June 2024 report could not be fetched.
I looked for a single independent count of how many of the 7 October dead were killed by Israeli fire and found only the passing statements in contested; no full accounting.

Hamas's 'Our Narrative' document itself could not be read at a Hamas or primary host; its words are taken from excerpts reproduced by the Counter Extremism Project and from the Jewish Chronicle, Times of Israel and Al-Monitor (AFP). The Jewish Chronicle and Times of Israel pieces are critical in tone; the Al-Monitor piece also quotes analysts' views.

skeptic.notes: Round 2: re-read every changed source and checked bylines on all news sources across the four cards. Fact 1 now has three independent wires (AP counted once for PBS and CBC, Reuters, AFP via JusticeInfo, which reports 251 hostages) plus HRW. Fact 6 (Hamas's own account): I read the Hamas text as reproduced by CEP; every phrase in the fact ('only targeted the occupation soldiers and those who carried weapons', 'religious and moral commitment', 'accidently', 'maybe some faults happened' via AFP/Al-Monitor) is on its page. All four outlets and CEP draw on one Hamas document, which was read in full through the CEP copy, so I count it as one source read several times, not four: nit. I reworded the last sentence of fact 6 from 'contradict the claim' (an editorial inference) to a statement of what the other facts report. Added wire AFP to the Dawn source in contested. Set CEP in contested to kind advocacy. Numbers rechecked against pages: 1,195 (Israeli government), 1,124 with 295 military (OHCHR), 815 of 1,195 (AFP via HRW), 251 hostages, 14 civilians (UN Commission). Fact 0's counts all trace to Israeli government figures; the card says so. Strongest objection from critics of Israel: the answer's only Hamas sentence is Hamas's denial of targeting; the Hannibal and unfounded-accounts points are in contested. Strongest from defenders: the answer states Hamas's account in one line while the findings take four; but each is attributed. Both stand. [should-fix] first heard quote is Hamas's weaker line; [should-fix] the strongest form of 'resistance' (right to armed struggle) and the legal answer is not a fact; [nit] fact 6 is one document.
